issue.body:
I know extending configurations similarly to what jsHint does was argued early in the project and the current solution is to just propagate options down the tree. This has some unwanted side effects, though.

A lot of JavaScript projects have structure loosely resembling this one:

```
├─┬ app
│ └── files for the browser
├─┬ dist
│ └── files for the browser
├─┬ test
│ ├── unit tests - executed in a browser
│ └── e2e tests - executed in Node
├── Gruntfile.js - for Node
└── karma.conf.js - for Node
```

This means that there has to be the `.eslintrc` file contained in the top project scope and it has to have the `node` environment enabled. But that means `"node": true` is also the default for `app`/`dist`/`test/unit`/etc. and has to be explicitly disabled in each of them separately which is easy to forget about (or even not think about it being needed).

OTH, if instead of cascading environments one could extend a file with base config for the whole project, all these workarounds would be unnecessary.

issue.title: [[FEAT]] Support .jshintrc "extends" with no specific path.

repository.name: jshint
repository.description: JSHint is a tool that helps to detect errors and potential problems in your JavaScript code

issue.body:
Extending the abilities of the .jshintrc file option `"extends"`.
The new behavior resembles the `root` option of .editorconfig files.

When the boolean value `true` is used:
JSHint will walk up the directory tree and look for a .jshintrc file.

If no .jshintrc file is found (root directory reached):
Nothing will happen, and the original .jshintrc file will be used as is.

If a .jshintrc file is found:
JSHint will behave as if the file's path was explicitly passed as the `"extends"` option.
This includes recursive behavior for this feature.
